solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tennis champion coming round to destroy shrub

indicators.note: the champion's name comes round, enclosing the word for destroy

parts.note: Rod Laver, Australian tennis champion who won two calendar Grand Slams
to end something is to destroy it

explanation.surface: A tennis star circles back to rip out a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender is a fragrant Mediterranean bush with purple flower spikes.

clue.text: Very many soldiers

definitions.meaning: a huge number, as in 'their name is ...'
a Roman army unit of several thousand troops

explanation.definitionFit: Legion means both a multitude and a large military unit.

clue.text: Bones on green and English hillside

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry
brae is Scots for a hillside

explanation.surface: Bones found on a grassy English slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertebrae are the small bones making up the spine.

clue.text: One German standing with outwardly carefree relative

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means read from the bottom, so reversed

parts.note: ein is German for one

indicators.note: only the outside letters are used

explanation.surface: A German stands beside a relaxed member of the family.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is the daughter of one's brother or sister.

clue.text: Gamines composing puzzles

indicators.note: composing means putting together, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Elfin girls are writing riddles.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmas are mysteries or riddles that baffle.

clue.text: Wattle from a state company in Italy

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California, a US state
C.ia is the Italian abbreviation for compagnia, company

explanation.surface: Australian wattle sourced from a US state firm operating in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Italian business names write 'and company' as 'e C.ia', so 'company in Italy' gives CIA, not the spy agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattle is the Australian name for trees of the acacia genus.

clue.text: Angered worker eating one roll

indicators.note: the outer letters take in the inner one, as if swallowing it

parts.note: cross means angry
I is the Roman numeral for one
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A furious labourer munches a bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is a crescent-shaped flaky pastry roll.

clue.text: Petrol makes this on board

parts.note: and the goods carried aboard a ship

explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the freight a ship or plane carries.

clue.text: Referring to uninspiring upset in poor gain

indicators.note: the turned word goes inside the shuffled letters
poor signals the letters are badly arranged
in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down

parts.note: dull means uninspiring

explanation.surface: Mentioning a dreary reversal in a small profit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' means turned upside down, i.e. read bottom to top; 'poor' is the anagram signal on gain, and 'in' places one piece within the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Alluding means mentioning something indirectly.

clue.text: Poor drainage for shrub

indicators.note: poor work is badly made, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Bad drainage is no good for a flowering bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardenia is an evergreen bush with fragrant white flowers.

clue.text: Light-chestnut horse in dock?

definitions.meaning: a horse of reddish-brown colouring is so named
the plant genus Rumex includes both docks and this sour-leaved herb, so it is a kind of dock

explanation.surface: A pale chestnut horse standing in the dock.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrel names both a reddish-brown horse colour and a sour-leaved herb of the dock family.

clue.text: Crispin, the old blackleg

definitions.meaning: St Crispin is patron saint of shoemakers
an archaic term for a strikebreaker

explanation.surface: Crispin was a scab in his day.
explanation.definitionFit: Snob once meant a cobbler and also a worker who refused to strike.

clue.text: Daisy, neat viewer

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
the organ one views with

explanation.surface: Daisy is a tidy observer.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxeye is a large wild daisy with white petals and a yellow centre.

clue.text: Poisonous plant from Trappist is criminal

parts.note: a Trappist is a monk of a strict Cistercian order
's is the short form of is
a hood is a gangster or criminal

explanation.surface: A deadly plant comes from a silent monk who turns out to be a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkshood, or aconite, is a highly toxic plant with hooded purple flowers.

clue.text: Flower occurs all over the place in spring

indicators.note: scattered everywhere, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A bloom pops up everywhere when spring comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in spring' adds nothing to the wordplay: it describes when the flower appears.
explanation.definitionFit: The crocus is a small bulb plant that blooms early in spring.

clue.text: Finch that's brought in Chancery suit

definitions.meaning: a bird whose crossed mandibles prise open cones
a bill filed by a defendant against the plaintiff in an old Chancery case

explanation.surface: A bird that is named in a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbill is a finch, and a cross-bill was a defendant's counter-bill in Chancery.

clue.text: Fern Britain giving account to Doddy

parts.note: Doddy was the nickname of comedian Ken Dodd

explanation.surface: Fern Britton gives a report on comedian Ken Dodd.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Dodd was a much-loved Liverpool comedian known affectionately as Doddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracken is a common coarse fern covering hillsides and heaths.

clue.text: Avoid castle without knocking over fences

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle
a show jumper who knocks no fences down goes clear

explanation.surface: Steer clear of the fortress unless your horse jumps cleanly.
explanation.walkthrough: In show jumping a clear round is one with no fences knocked down.
explanation.definitionFit: Keep clear is an idiom for staying away from something.

clue.text: Norm and precocious girl swapping notes for Italian food

parts.note: par is the norm or standard

indicators.note: one musical note letter is exchanged for another

parts.note: a madam is a cheeky, precocious girl

explanation.surface: Norm and a forward girl trade messages over Italian dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: D is a note; H is B natural in German notation, so 'swapping notes' replaces D in MADAM with H to give MAHAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Parma ham is a cured Italian ham from the Parma region.

clue.text: Strange name on single flower

indicators.note: something strange is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: An odd name for a single bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' is the anagram signal on name; 'on' just joins the pieces, as one sits above the other in a down-style reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Anemone, the windflower, is a garden bloom of the buttercup family.

clue.text: Former partner's morning test

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
a.m. means morning

explanation.surface: An ex sets a morning trial.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal test of knowledge.

clue.text: Beer spilt around books on Hindus' sacred plant

indicators.note: the shuffled beer letters go around the abbreviation for books
spilt liquid ends up scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Beer is splashed over the books lying by a holy tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilt' is the anagram signal on Beer, and 'around' wraps those letters round the books.
explanation.definitionFit: The bo tree is the sacred fig under which the Buddha gained enlightenment, revered by Hindus too.

clue.text: Composer in libel trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer finds himself in a defamation case.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincenzo Bellini was an Italian opera composer, author of Norma.

clue.text: Entertainment from comic, in email

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of these words

explanation.surface: Fun comes from a funny email.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinema is film shown as public entertainment.

clue.text: Materials ordered for marsh plant

indicators.note: put in order, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Supplies are sent for to deal with a bog plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mare's-tail is an aquatic plant with whorled leaves growing in ponds and marshes.

clue.text: Two coins for relaxation

parts.note: the rand is the South African currency
R stands for rand or rupee, another coin

explanation.surface: A pair of coins buys some downtime.
explanation.definitionFit: R and R stands for rest and recuperation.

clue.text: Plants first cut before start of play

indicators.note: the first letter of cut is taken

parts.note: Act I is the opening of a stage play

explanation.surface: Greenery is trimmed back before a game begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacti are spiny succulent plants of dry regions.

clue.text: Flic upset holding notice for recruit

indicators.note: the turned word holds the notice inside it
in a down clue upset turns the word upside down

parts.note: flic is French slang for a policeman; tec is a detective
an ad is a notice

explanation.surface: A French cop is annoyed at holding a notice for a new recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flic' is French police slang; the English equivalent tec is turned up by 'upset' in this down clue, then 'holding' takes in the notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young trainee in the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Speedwell obtained from the bin …

indicators.note: the answer is got out of these letters by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A wild flower recovered from the rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the next clue, which gives another speedwell name.
explanation.definitionFit: Henbit speedwell is the ivy-leaved speedwell, a low weed of cultivated ground.

clue.text: … and another for Primrose and Clarence

definitions.meaning: following the previous clue, another kind of speedwell
a small pink primula of northern limestone grassland
Clarence ..., the American who pioneered frozen food

explanation.surface: Another one for two people called Primrose and Clarence.
explanation.walkthrough: Primrose and Clarence look like people's names; one is a flower, the other the frozen-food founder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bird's-eye names a speedwell, a primula species and the frozen-food founder Clarence Birdseye.

clue.text: Evergreen cut back in barrel — try mulching a little

indicators.note: the extract is read from right to left
the letters lie within the words that follow
only a small part of the words is used

explanation.surface: Prune an evergreen in a tub and mulch it lightly.
explanation.walkthrough: ELTRYM sits inside 'barrel — try mulching' and, read backwards, gives the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an aromatic evergreen shrub sacred to Venus.

clue.text: Know about river climber

parts.note: wist is an archaic past form of wit, to know

indicators.note: about signals the river's name turned round

parts.note: the Aire is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: A mountaineer is familiar with the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisteria is a woody climbing plant with hanging lilac flower clusters.
